# Set-ZbxCepRule

## SYNOPSIS

Changes an event processing rule.

## SYNTAX

```
Set-ZbxCepRule [-InputObject] <ZabbixReference<ZabbixCepRule>[]> [[-Name] <string>] [-Filter <ZabbixCepRuleFilterRequest>] [-WindowType <ZabbixCepRuleWindowType>] [-Window <ZabbixCepRuleWindowRequest>] [-Operation <ZabbixCepRuleOperationRequest[]>] [-Stop <ZabbixCepRuleExecution>] [-Position <int>] [-Description <string>] [-Status <ZabbixCepRuleStatus>] [-AdditionalProperty <Hashtable>] [-Force] [-PassThru] [-PipedRecord <PSObject>] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

An event processing rule matches incoming events against a filter within a time window and applies its operations to them, in sort order (Zabbix 8.0 and later). The Set-ZbxCepRule cmdlet changes the event processing rules given to -InputObject (names, ids or piped objects) with ceprule.update; a field whose parameter is not given keeps its value. Every event processing rule the pipeline brings is changed in one call when the pipeline ends, and -AdditionalProperty sets any other field by its API name. The command writes nothing unless -PassThru is given, which reads the changed event processing rules back and writes them; -WhatIf shows what would change.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Change an event processing rule

```powershell
Set-ZbxCepRule -InputObject 'Tag web alerts' -Status Disabled
```

Disables the event processing rule Tag web alerts, so incoming events skip it.

### Example 2: Change an event processing rule and write the result

```powershell
Set-ZbxCepRule -InputObject 'Tag web alerts' -Status Disabled -PassThru
```

The same change with -PassThru, which reads the event processing rule Tag web alerts back from the server and writes it; without it the command writes nothing.
